Claude format (/v1/messages) also accepts an x-api-key header; Gemini format (/v1beta/models/...) accepts an x-goog-api-key header or a ?key= query parameter. Failures use the OpenAI error envelope: A single token reaches every upstream provider aggregated by the platform. The APIs fall into four protocol families: Which models a token can call is decided by its group, the token's model allowlist and the model's billing configuration. Always use the model names returned by GET /v1/models; do not guess model IDs. - When a request is accepted, quota is pre-deducted from the model price and the estimated usage, then settled against the actual usage. Failed requests and tasks that produced no output are refunded. - Insufficient quota returns 403; rate limiting or saturated upstream concurrency returns 429; an unknown model or no channel available in the current group returns 503. - Image generation count n is capped at 128. Video duration, resolution and batch size follow the selected model's limits; out-of-range requests are rejected before acceptance. /v1/files, /v1/fine-tunes, /v1/images/variations and DELETE /v1/models/{model} currently return 501. Do not call them in production.

b: Before wiring a model into Uter, verify it step by step — can it connect, can it answer, is it stable, is it billed correctly — so problems surface before production. Start with the Playground in the console, then re-check over the API. That split quickly separates “the model is unavailable” from “my request is wrong”. Confirm you have the items below. Missing any one of them makes step 1 fail. - Group: determines billing ratio and the routable model set. A key bills and routes according to its group. - Channel: the upstream provider that actually serves a model (e.g. Uter channel, aggregate channel, shared channel). One model can be served by several enabled channels, or by a single one. The same model can therefore differ in availability and price across groups and over time. “No available channel” means no enabled channel currently serves that model for your group — not that your request is malformed. An API key is a password: use it only server-side or in a secret manager. Never send it to a browser, never log it in plaintext, never commit it. API keys have four states: Enabled, Disabled, Expired, Exhausted. Creating or editing a key can also apply: - Expiry: “Never expires” by default; after expiry calls return 401. - Quota cap: a dedicated allowance or “Unlimited”. When used up the key becomes Exhausted. - Model limits: allow only selected models. With no model selected the key cannot call anything. - IP allowlist: supports CIDR (e.g. 203.0.113.0/24); other sources are rejected. - Allow querying user quota: whether this key may call /v1/dashboard/billing/. Console → Playground exercises the same model path as the API. 1. Pick a channel on the left; the right pane lists that channel's models. Select the model to test. 2.
